newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Basic eyes tie-up with PetroVietnam.
newsitem.headline: Basic eyes tie-up with PetroVietnam.

text.p: Philippine oil driller Basic Petroleum and Minerals Inc is eyeing a joint venture with PetroVietnam for the setting up of downstream energy facilities in Vietnam.
Basic president Oscar de Venecia told Reuters Basic is looking at a tie-up with PetroVietnam involving a petrochemical plant plants and gasoline stations.
De Venecia said he met with PetroVietnam officials at a meeting last week of members of the ASEAN Chamber of Commerce and Industry.
"We will conduct further talks with them in October. We are studying the matter carefully in line with our thrust of diversification and globalisation," de Venecia said.
"We are also awaiting the passage of legislation in Vietnam which will put in place additional incentives for investors," he added.
De Venecia said Basic will pursue talks with financing companies for the possible joint venture with PetroVietnam.
PetroVietnam is planning a 450,000 tonne per year naphtha cracker, polypropylene and polyethylene plants with a capacity of 200,000 tonnes each and some 500 to 700 gasoline stations, he said.
De Venecia said Basic may join PetroVietnam in any of these ventures.
